Exercise: Flat Bench Lying Leg Raise

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- abdominal_contraction
- isolated_hip_flexion

Primary Muscles:

- abdominals

Secondary Muscles:
None

Equipment:

- bodyweight

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- core_strength_and_stability
- abdominal_muscle_definition

Contraindications:

- Lower back pain
- Recent abdominal surgery

Exercise Variations:

- name: Hanging Leg Raise, equipment: bar or pull-up bar
- name: Seated Leg Raise, equipment: seated position on a bench

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Bicycle Crunches, equipment: body only
- exercise_name: Leg Raises on V-Machine, equipment: V-machine

Instructions:

- Lie with your back flat on a bench and your legs extended in front of you off the end.
- Place your hands either under your glutes with your palms down or by the sides holding on to the bench. This will be your starting position.
- As you keep your legs extended, straight as possible with your knees slightly bent but locked raise your legs until they make a 90-degree angle with the floor. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and hold the contraction at the top for a second.
- Now, as you inhale, slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
